page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores across two threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache distribution provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache pool. Architectural extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions, as well as BMI2 and ADX. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached persistent disks for storage operations.

Benchmark outcomes show sharp divergence between single-threaded efficiency and aggregate multi-core throughput. Stress-ng single-core performance scores 2,864.78, ranking within the top 25% of evaluated cloud systems. Conversely, stress-ng multi-core registers at 5,737.06, placing in the bottom 25% due to the 4-vCPU ceiling. Geekbench results echo this divide, achieving an average 1,764.0 in single-core tests against a bottom-quartile 3,748.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory-intensive benchmarks reveal performance limitations when accessing larger arrays: while cached 16 KB read-only memory bandwidth delivers 282.49 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB reads and writes fall to 20.8 GB/sec and 11.76 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%.

Application-level measurements indicate suitability for moderate data operations with modest concurrency requirements. The instance achieves 5.46 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 5.89 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark database operations register at 1,960.11, while standard PassMark CPU and memory marks reach 7,014.33 and 2,304.87 respectively. For lightweight machine learning workloads, inference speeds using a small 135M model maintain average metrics of 434.85 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 138.57 tokens/sec for generation, though throughput drops sharply to 10.94 and 7.78 tokens/sec on 7B models.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory allocation makes the c3d-highmem-4 a cost-efficient resource tier for memory-bound applications that do not require extensive parallel compute. Workload profiles that benefit most from this topology include in-memory key-value caches, intermediate database tiers, ETL staging buffers, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores) on an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor and 32.0 GB of RAM. The instance features an elevated 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. It provisions no local storage and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark profiles reveal strong single-thread performance, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng, alongside middle-tier Geekbench and PassMark baseline ratings. However, total multi-threaded throughput and large-block uncached memory bandwidth fall in the lower quartiles due to the limited core count and memory bus constraints. c3d-highmem-4 is functionally best suited for workloads requiring higher RAM density than compute capacity, such as intermediate in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, ETL staging, and low-concurrency data services.
